Subject: Hosted API: proposed commit uplift & early-renewal incentive

Lisa —

Appreciate the numbers. Attached is a concise proposal for a 250M tokens/month committed plan, with two structure options: 12-month early-renewal (10% usage credit + reduced per-token unit) or 24-month reserved (15% credit and a deeper unit discount). Key bullets:

- Proposed commit: 250M tokens/month baseline
- Rate tiers: base unit = $0.0006/token, >200M tier = $0.00052/token (applies to overage after commit)
- Early-renewal incentive: 10% credit applied to first 3 billing cycles if signed before 2026-11-15
- Burst allowance: up to 30% burst capacity for 48 hours with automatic throttling to maintain SLOs
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated routing; Hosted SLAs available in contract addendum

I included a simple retention/credit example in the attached Excel so you can model cost vs forecast. If this looks reasonable, we can prepare a formal quote and a DocuSign package for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_commit_sheet_20261002.xlsx (pricing table + examples)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Your team confirms preferred term (12 vs 24) and target start month
2) Redwood issues formal quote + SOW draft
3) Procurement confirms PO timing; we prepare DocuSign for signatures

Looping Karthik on rate-limit/throughput notes below.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa@finserve.co>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: proposed commit uplift & early-renewal incentive

Hi team — quick technical clarifications from infra/ops so expectations are aligned:

- Rate-limits: for the 250M commit with burst allowance we recommend a sustained per-tenant QPS cap of 220 requests/sec with short-term bursting to 600 rps using autoscaling policy.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile generation latency expected to remain under 280ms for typical prompt lengths (<= 1k tokens) on Hosted deployment when routed to Dedicated pools.
- Caching: we can enable prefix cache for FinServe workloads which reduces token billing on repeated prompts (we'll provide cache hit metrics during onboarding).
- Fallbacks: if regional capacity is constrained, policy will route to compatible model variant — we'll surface any quality deltas in the release notes.

If you approve the commit numbers, ops will pre-configure autoscaling rules and a canary route to validate production traffic before full traffic shift.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
